item.title: Hackers abused Claude to extract secrets from 1.8M Android apps
item.description: Problem: A threat actor used Claude to automate mass extraction of hardcoded secrets from Android apps. Approach: The attacker's pipeline downloaded 1.8 million APKs, decompiled them, and scanned for secrets with TruffleHog, using Claude to help automate collection and triage at scale. Result: Over 100 secret types found; 2,100+ Azure AD tokens pulled from 40+ corporate tenants in 34 hours; some breaches reached full admin control in under 3 hours. Why it matters: AI automation compresses recon-to-compromise time dramatically, exposing a governance gap in how these platforms get used and abused. Glossary: APK (Android app package); decompile (convert compiled code back to readable form); hardcoded secret (credential baked into code); Azure AD token (Microsoft cloud login credential).

item.title: GitLab urges users to patch max severity path traversal flaw
item.description: Problem: CVE-2026-85706, a maximum-severity, unauthenticated path traversal flaw in GitLab's repository commits API. Approach: Attackers send a crafted POST request with a manipulated file path to the commits API, bypassing authentication and path checks to read arbitrary files off the server. Result: Security firm watchTowr observed in-the-wild scanning within 24 hours of disclosure. GitLab shipped patched versions (19.3.2, 19.2.6, 19.1) the same week. Why it matters: GitLab runs at over half of Fortune 100 companies; unauthenticated arbitrary file read can leak credentials and proprietary data at massive scale if left unpatched. Glossary: path traversal (accessing files outside an intended directory); unauthenticated (no login required); API endpoint (a specific URL for programmatic requests); CVE (a public vulnerability ID).
